editorial:
Imagine a world where you can legally hire a professional killer to take out the person who ruined your life. That is the wild setup here. You follow a high-stakes game of cat and mouse in a futuristic Japan where revenge is a government-backed business. The vibe is gritty and tense, focusing on the clash between the executioners and the guards who try to protect the targets. It feels like a dark comic book brought to life, mixing a strange legal system with a lot of street-level violence and emotional weight.

What really hits home is the action and the way the tension builds up. The fights are raw, and the plot keeps you guessing about who is actually the good guy. While some parts of the story feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you love stylized action, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older flick, try to find a high-quality 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see the details clearly, or look for a high-res rental on Apple TV to get the best picture possible.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a heavy emotional punch. After a series of brutal fights, the main characters face the truth about their shared past. The cycle of revenge finally breaks when the protagonist realizes that killing the target does not actually heal the pain. It ends with a bittersweet feeling, showing that while the law allows for vengeance, it never truly brings peace to the victims or the killers.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark revenge stories and stylized Japanese action movies.
